# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Sorokyne Strata for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it. Every flag that has flown here tells it a little differently.[/italic]
## A Cold Find An automated probe catalogued LV-976 in 2112: a frozen world around a dim red dwarf, with gravity a quarter stronger than Earth's and one airless, irradiated rock for a neighbour. It sits in a narrow strip of neutral space between the Union of Progressive Peoples and the United Americas, and more than one party filed a claim to it. [bold]Weyland-Yutani[/bold] backed its own claim with a colony ship in 2152.
## The Outpost, 2163 - The research outpost was founded in 2163. A second outpost for the mines followed, along with permanent housing for the research staff. - Construction and security went to [bold]Sestra Solutions[/bold], a UPP-aligned firm. Its checkpoints, at the landing zones, on the decks and at the armoured gate to the north, are still the first thing a new arrival meets.
## Two Outposts, Two Languages The labs filled with Company contractors and colonists from the Americas. The mine levels filled with Union contract crews. Shift notices went up in one language and went unread on the other side of the outpost, and in 2166 a canteen cook and a mine level clerk began copying every notice out by hand in both. Those sheets were the first Herald, and the paper sheet still carries every headline twice.
## Into the Crust, 2171 From 2171 the colony turned to terraforming the thermal tunnels that run through the planet's crust. Heat from the core was put to work, and below the ice there are now warm marshes, hot springs, Carp Lake and the jungle around the Botanical Research Station. The colony is now reckoned to be worth billions. Nobody has yet told the Herald what goes on in the research station that has no name on its door.
## Living Side by Side Workers from rival powers share one canteen, one bar and one basketball court, and most days that is enough. Some days it is not. When tempers rise, the Herald prints what happened in both languages, so that nobody can tell their own side a different story.
